source: docs/agent-log.md: the author's .git exposure fix was bypassable on Windows; found by reviewer
prompt: A colleague says that on their Windows machine, `curl --path-as-is "http://127.0.0.1:5500/js/..%5c.git/config"` returns our git config from the QueryIt dev server, even though server.js is supposed to only serve index.html, css/ and js/. Can you check and fix it?
expected: resolvePublicFile in server.js decides on a POSIX-normalized string: %5c decodes to a backslash, path.posix.normalize does not treat it as a separator, so 'js/..\.git/config' passes the js/ prefix check, then path.join (win32) collapses it to ROOT\.git\config. A good agent reproduces it against a running server on a free port (or a unit probe) before fixing, fixes it by deciding on the resolved filesystem path (path.resolve + path.relative, checking the first segment) and/or rejecting backslash, ':' (alternate data streams) and NUL, adds regression tests for %5c variants and ::$DATA, keeps legitimate paths working (/, /index.html, /js/app.js, /js/lib/../app.js), and stops every server it started.

rubric.criterion: Reproduced the bypass (request returning the file, or a probe of resolvePublicFile) before fixing
Explained the cause (decision on a string normalized differently from how the path is resolved) and fixed it at the cause, not by blacklisting only the exact '%5c.git' string
Covered variants: other files (package.json, .claude/), ::$DATA / colon, and kept legitimate paths working
Added regression tests in test/servers.test.js (or equivalent) that fail without the fix
Stopped any servers it started and did not leave the environment in a broken state
Accurate report: cause, reproduction, fix, verification
